reason: The central measurement is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that inverts the consequence. Driven at ?motion=play, 1440x960, sampling every focusable (a[href], button, [tabindex]) with ancestor opacity multiplied in: every focusable ELEMENT is at effective opacity >= 0.1 at 192ms after __LATELY_READY, >= 0.5 at 242ms, >= 0.9 at 360ms. Not 1203ms, and nothing is below 0.1 at 900ms - the seat's 'still 3 at 900ms' is false. I reproduced the seat's 1203ms figure exactly (1193ms) only by multiplying in getComputedStyle(el, '::before').opacity, which proves what was actually measured: .dot::before, the decorative disc. The disc is not the focusable and does not carry the ring. lately.html:301 says so in the source comment - 'The disc is a pseudo, not the button' - a deliberate earlier fix so the control's geometry survives its own entrance. The .dot button is fully laid out from the first frame; .dot:focus-visible paints 2px solid #4f46e5 at offset 3px on it (verified computed on a focused dot at t=59ms), and focusing a dot also fires show(el), raising the tooltip with the job title - the tip is outside #root, carries no rise, and is at full opacity. So on the dots, which are 9 of the 12 controls the seat counted, focus is not only visible, it is annotated. The claim that there is 'no way to tell whether focus has entered the page' is contradicted by the surface. What is left is the KPI links, and their exposure is unreachable in practice. The tab sequence opens with three static header tab links (lately.html:720-722) at opacity 1, which absorb Tabs 1-3, so a person's first Tab always lands on painted ink. Tab 4 reaches a.kpi.rise, whose worst delay is 65ms with a 500ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) ease-out. Driving four presses at 40ms apart - faster than any keyboard's autorepeat first interval, which is 250-500ms - lands at opacity 0.805; at 80ms, 0.993; at 150ms, 1.000. The seat's 'opacity 0.000' reproduces only by firing four presses inside 8ms, which is a Playwright artefact, not a human input path. The residue is real but tiny: for roughly the first 190ms the ring on a KPI card is dimmed rather than absent. That is a refinement, not a defect, and an overstated class is on its own grounds for refusal here. The seat is right that interaction-check.mjs:107-117 evaluates 'nothing invisible can take focus' on the settled surface using the element's own computed opacity, so this transient has never been gated - but a blind gate is only worth a finding if something is behind it, and what is behind it is 190ms of a fading ring on cards that Tab cannot reach that fast.
sharpenedFix: The proposed fix is wrong twice over and should not land as written. (1) The code is buggy: { capture: true, once: true } removes the listener on the FIRST keydown of ANY key, with the e.key === 'Tab' guard running inside it - so Escape (which this surface already binds at lately.html:949) or any stray key burns the listener and the Tab case never fires again. (2) The behaviour is worse than the symptom. A human's first Tab typically arrives 300ms-1s in, by which time the rise is finished but the meters (delay 620-860ms), the nine dot pops (760-1200ms) and the best-week record draw (1.1s) are all mid-flight. Snapping data-motion='settled' at that instant makes five meter bars jump to final width, nine discs appear from nothing and a dashed ceiling line materialise simultaneously - a large peripheral jump at the exact moment the user is hunting for the ring. It also does not touch the thing the seat actually measured, and data-motion='settled' is permanent for the session while the hero count-up is a JS rAF loop the [data-motion] block does not cover, so the figure keeps ticking after everything else has snapped. If the panel wants belt-and-braces on the 190ms residue, the correct shape is one CSS rule, no JS and no global snap: let the element that receives focus finish instantly while everything else keeps its choreography - 'a.kpi:focus-visible { animation: none; opacity: 1; transform: none; }' and, for controls whose animated ancestor is the card, '.card.rise:focus-within, .limit.rise:focus-within { animation: none; opacity: 1; transform: none; }'. Honest recommendation: this is optional polish, not a fix that is owed.
breaks: The seat's fix would break the entrance for every keyboard user who Tabs during it (mass snap of meters, dots and record line), and would make the choreography unobservable to any future gate assertion that drives ?motion=play and also presses a key. If either fix lands, re-measure: interaction-check.mjs's motion-contract trio at lines 518-521 ('the entrance actually runs when it is asked to', 'the figure counts up from below and never overshoots', 'the previous best draws last') - none of them press keys today, so they should stay green, but the seat's version makes them one keypress away from false; interaction-check.mjs:117 'nothing invisible can take focus' across all seven states; and audit.mjs's motion budget and WCAG contrast pass, since a :focus-within rule that cancels a card's entrance changes the composited backdrop the contrast check samples. Frame reproducibility is unaffected either way - the 56 frames are captured at the webdriver default of settled, where animation-duration is already 1ms.
